items.title: Smooth projective analytifications have rational Kähler forms
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), inherited from the Jacobian-criterion, embedding and Chern-form suppliers below. Let $X$ be a smooth projective complex scheme of pure dimension $n$. Then the closed points of $X$ carry a structure of **compact Hausdorff second-countable smooth complex manifold** $X^{\mathrm{an}}$ of complex dimension $n$, its analytification, such that: every standard smooth algebraic chart of $X$ becomes a holomorphic chart of $X^{\mathrm{an}}$, and every morphism of smooth complex schemes $X\to Y$ induces a holomorphic map $X^{\mathrm{an}}\to Y^{\mathrm{an}}$. Moreover, for every ample invertible sheaf $A$ on $X$ there is a smooth positive closed real $(1,1)$-form $\eta_A$ on $X^{\mathrm{an}}$ whose de Rham class is the real image of the topological first Chern class $c_1(A):=c_1(A^{\mathrm{an}})\in H^2(X^{\mathrm{an}};\mathbb Z)$: $$J_{X^{\mathrm{an}}}[\eta_A]=\rho_{X^{\mathrm{an}}}\bigl(c_1(A)\bigr),$$ where $J$ is the de Rham comparison and $\rho$ the change of coefficients $\mathbb Z\to\mathbb R$.
items.strategy:
Assume AC. Route: build the analytic charts from the relative Jacobian criterion and the holomorphic implicit function theorem, get compactness from a projective embedding into $\mathbb P^N(\mathbb C)$, and build the form from the Fubini-Study metric; sources: Serre, GAGA, §1 n°5 and §2 n°5-7 (Lemme 1, Proposition 2, Corollaire 3, Proposition 6, printed pp. 8-12), and Demailly, Chapter V §12 (12.2)-(12.8), §13 (13.2)-(13.4), §15.B (15.8) and Theorem (15.10), Chapter VI §4 (4.4)-(4.6). Step 1 (charts). The morphism $X	o\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C$ is locally of finite presentation, so at a closed point $x$ the relative Jacobian criterion [[thm-jacobian-criterion-smooth-morphism]] gives a standard smooth presentation $C_h\cong(\mathbb C[t_1,\dots,t_m]/(f_1,\dots,f_r))_g$ in which some $r	imes r$ minor of the Jacobian is invertible at $x$; the chart is flat over $\mathbb C$ with geometrically regular fibres of dimension $m-r$, and pure dimension $n$ of $X$ over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C$ gives $m-r=n$. On complex points the minor remains invertible on a Euclidean neighbourhood, and the holomorphic implicit function theorem [[thm-holomorphic-implicit-function-theorem]] presents the common zero set of $f_1,\dots,f_r$ as a holomorphic graph over $n$ coordinates, a chart of a complex manifold of dimension $n$ ([[def-complex-manifolds-and-holomorphic-vector-bundles]]). Two such charts are related by isomorphisms of localized standard smooth $\mathbb C$-algebras; their coordinate functions are rational functions with nonvanishing denominators near the point, hence holomorphic, and the inverse transition is holomorphic by the holomorphic inverse function theorem in several variables [[thm-holomorphic-inverse-function-theorem-several-variables]]. The charts glue on their overlaps, and morphisms of smooth complex schemes become holomorphic because their chart expressions are regular. Step 2 (compactness and topology). By [[thm-ample-powers-very-ample-proper-base]] with $S=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C$ (Noetherian), $X$ proper of finite type over $S$ and $A$ ample, some $A^{\otimes d}$ is closed $H$-very ample relative to $S$: there is a closed immersion $j:X	o\mathbb P^N_{\mathbb C}$ with $j^*\mathcal O(1)\cong A^{\otimes d}$. The complex points $\mathbb P^N(\mathbb C)$ are a compact Hausdorff second-countable complex manifold [[def-complex-projective-space-and-holomorphic-charts]]; the defining homogeneous equations of $j$ have full-rank holomorphic Jacobian along $X(\mathbb C)$, so by Step 1's graph presentation $j^{\mathrm{an}}$ identifies the manifold topology of $X^{\mathrm{an}}$ with the subspace topology of a closed subset of $\mathbb P^N(\mathbb C)$; that subset is closed (it is a common zero locus of polynomials) and hence compact. Closed subspaces of second-countable Hausdorff spaces are second-countable Hausdorff, and the local dimension is $n$. Step 3 (the form). Put $\omega_{\mathrm{FS}}= rac{i}{2\pi}\partial ar\partial\log(1+|z|^2)$ on the standard chart of $\mathbb P^N(\mathbb C)$; chart changes add $\log|g|^2$ for a nonvanishing holomorphic $g$, whose $\partial ar\partial$ vanishes, so the local forms glue to a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form whose Hermitian matrix $ igl((1+|z|^2)\delta_{jk}- ar z_jz_k igr)/ igl(2\pi(1+|z|^2)^2 igr)$ is positive definite by Cauchy-Schwarz ([[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]]). items.title: Kähler identities give Lefschetz sl-two and hard Lefschetz
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), inherited from the analytic suppliers below. Let $X$ be a compact Kähler $n$-fold with Kähler form $\omega$, in the conventions of [[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]], and put $L=[\omega]\smile(-)$ on cohomology. Then $L^{n-k}:H^k(X;\mathbb R)\to H^{2n-k}(X;\mathbb R)$ is an isomorphism for $0\le k\le n$. Harmonic representatives transport $(L,\Lambda,H)$ to an $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ action: here $\Lambda$ on cohomology means applying $\Lambda$ to the harmonic representative, not to an arbitrary closed form, and $H$ acts by $\deg-n$. Primitive cohomology is $P^k=\ker L^{n-k+1}$, and $$H^k(X;\mathbb R)=\bigoplus_{r\ge\max(0,k-n)}L^rP^{k-2r},$$ with the type decomposition inherited from forms: a class of type $(p,q)$ has primitive components of type $(p-r,q-r)$. If $[\omega]$ is the real image of a rational class $\ell$, all these decompositions and $L$-isomorphisms are rational, and they remain isomorphisms after extension to every characteristic-zero field.
items.strategy: Assume AC. Route: transport the pointwise Hermitian-exterior algebra through the Hodge isomorphism; sources: Schnell, Class 18, Theorem 18.13 with Corollary 18.14 and the sl2 discussion, printed pp. 4-5; Demailly, Chapter VI §8.3 (8.13)-(8.17), printed p. 313; the pointwise input is [[lem-hermitian-exterior-lefschetz-decomposition-and-weil-star-identity]]. Step 1 (operators on cohomology). The Kähler commutators [[lem-kahler-commutators-and-laplacian-type-preservation]] give $[\Delta,L]=[\Delta,\Lambda]=0$, so $L$ and $\Lambda$ carry harmonic forms to harmonic forms. By the Hodge theorem [[thm-compact-kahler-hodge-decomposition-via-elliptic-harmonic-forms]] every de Rham class has a unique harmonic representative; define $L,\Lambda,H$ on $H^*(X;\mathbb R)$ by applying the corresponding operator to that representative. On closed forms $L$ is wedge with $\omega$, which descends on cohomology to cup product with $[\omega]$; the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ relations and $H=(\deg-n)$ hold on forms, hence on harmonic forms by commutation with $\Delta$, and pass to cohomology. Note that $\Lambda$ does not preserve closed forms in general, which is why it is transported through the harmonic representative. Step 2 (primitive decomposition and hard Lefschetz). By the unique primitive decomposition of [[lem-hermitian-exterior-lefschetz-decomposition-and-weil-star-identity]], every harmonic form $u$ of degree $k$ is uniquely $\sum_rL^ru_r$ with $u_r$ primitive harmonic of degree $k-2r$; the projections are polynomials in $L,\Lambda$, and the string formulas give $\Lambda^sL^ru=\frac{r!}{(r-s)!}\cdot\frac{(n-k-r+s)!}{(n-k-r)!}L^{r-s}u$ for $0\le s\le r\le n-k$ and $L^{n-k+1}u=0$ for primitive $u$ of degree $k$, while $L^ru\ne0$ for $0\le r\le n-k$. Hence $L^{n-k}:H^k\to H^{2n-k}$ is bijective for $k\le n$ (on each string it maps the lowest vector to the highest), the kernel of $L^{n-k+1}$ is exactly $P^k$, and the displayed direct sum follows by taking harmonic representatives summand by summand. As $L$ has bidegree $(1,1)$ and $\Lambda$ has bidegree $(-1,-1)$, a class of type $(p,q)$ has primitive components of type $(p-r,q-r)$. Step 3 (rationality). Suppose $[\omega]=\rho(\ell)$ with $\ell\in H^2(X;\mathbb Q)$. In rational bases the matrix of $L^{n-k}:H^k(X;\mathbb Q)\to H^{2n-k}(X;\mathbb Q)$ is rational; it becomes invertible over $\mathbb R$, so its determinant is a nonzero rational number and it is already invertible over $\mathbb Q$, remaining invertible after scalar extension to any characteristic-zero field $F$ under the comparison $H^*(X;\mathbb Q)\otimes F\cong H^*(X;F)$, which preserves cup products ([[lem-rational-cohomology-scalar-comparison-for-compact-smooth-manifolds]]). The kernels $P^k=\ker L^{n-k+1}$ are then rational, and downward induction on $k$ shows that the rational matrix of the direct-sum map $\bigoplus_{r\ge\max(0,k-n)}L^rP^{k-2r}\to H^k$ is invertible over $\mathbb Q$ because it becomes the isomorphism of Step 2 over $\mathbb R$; hence the decomposition is rational. Finally, the lowering operator reconstructed on a string by $\Lambda L^ru=r(n-k-r+1)L^{r-1}u$ has rational coefficients and coincides over $\mathbb R$ with the transported harmonic $\Lambda$ by uniqueness of the primitive decomposition.

items.title: Morphisms, polarizability and simplicity of rational Hodge structures
items.statement: With the conventions of [[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]], all structures in this item are rational pure Hodge structures of a fixed weight $k$. A **morphism of Hodge structures** $f:(V,\{V^{p,q}\})\to(W,\{W^{p,q}\})$ is a $\mathbb Q$-linear map $f:V\to W$ whose $\mathbb C$-linear extension satisfies $f_{\mathbb C}(V^{p,q})\subseteq W^{p,q}$ for all $p+q=k$. **Kernels and images** are again rational sub-Hodge structures: a bidegree-preserving map sends the bidegree components of a vector into the matching components, so $\ker(f_{\mathbb C})=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}\bigl(\ker(f_{\mathbb C})\cap V^{p,q}\bigr)$ and $\operatorname{im}(f_{\mathbb C})=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}\bigl(\operatorname{im}(f_{\mathbb C})\cap W^{p,q}\bigr)$, the second sum being direct because the target bidegrees $W^{p,q}$ are distinct. The **direct sum** is $(V\oplus W)^{p,q}=V^{p,q}\oplus W^{p,q}$, with the inclusions and projections as morphisms. A **short exact sequence** $0\to U\xrightarrow{i}V\xrightarrow{\pi}W\to 0$ of weight-$k$ Hodge structures consists of morphisms that are exact as a sequence of $\mathbb Q$-vector spaces; it **splits** in the category of Hodge structures if $\pi$ admits a morphism $s:W\to V$ with $\pi\circ s=\operatorname{id}_W$. A Hodge structure is **polarizable** if it admits a polarization, and **simple** if it has no nonzero proper rational sub-Hodge structure.
items.strategy: This item records the vocabulary invoked below on this page — the orthogonal splitting of polarized Hodge structures and the absolute projective Hodge package — as the pure weight-$k$ case of the morphisms of $\mathbb Q$-Hodge structures of Deligne, Théorie de Hodge II, (2.1.11)-(2.1.12), printed pp. 26-27. It is deliberately not routed through the mixed Hodge structures of a different page of this run, which lie outside this page's declared prerequisite closure. The only assertions to check are the componentwise closure claims recorded in the statement: if $x=\sum x^{p,q}$ and $f_{\mathbb C}(x)=0$, then $0=\sum f_{\mathbb C}(x^{p,q})$ with $f_{\mathbb C}(x^{p,q})\in W^{p,q}$, so every $f_{\mathbb C}(x^{p,q})=0$; and $\operatorname{im}(f_{\mathbb C})=\sum_{p+q=k}f_{\mathbb C}(V^{p,q})$ is direct because the target bidegrees are distinct. No proof phase applies to a definition, and no choice principle is used.
items.axiom_use: Choice-free: the item fixes definitions and verifies componentwise linear algebra; no choice principle is used.

items.title: Polarized rational Hodge structures split orthogonally
items.statement: Let $(V,Q)$ be a polarized rational pure Hodge structure and $U\subseteq V$ a rational sub-Hodge structure, with the notions of [[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]] and [[def-morphisms-and-polarizability-of-rational-hodge-structures]]. Then $Q|_U$ is a polarization of $U$, and $V=U\oplus U^{\perp_Q}$ is an orthogonal direct sum of rational Hodge structures in which the complement is polarized. Every short exact sequence of polarizable rational pure Hodge structures of a fixed weight splits in the category of Hodge structures, and every polarizable rational pure Hodge structure is a finite direct sum of simple Hodge structures. These are claims about rational Hodge substructures; they do not assert a splitting for an arbitrary local system. Every rational splitting persists after extension of scalars to any characteristic-zero field; no positivity or ordered-field structure on that field is asserted, and a subobject over an extension field need not be defined over $\mathbb Q$.
items.strategy: Choice-free finite-dimensional linear algebra. Route: Deligne, Théorie de Hodge II, (2.1.15)-(2.1.17), printed pp. 26-27, and Lemme (4.2.3) with its proof, printed p. 44. Step 1 (the restriction is a polarization). The Weil operator $C$ and complex conjugation preserve $U_{\mathbb C}$, because $U$ is a rational sub-Hodge structure. The form $h(x,y)=Q(Cx,\bar y)$ restricts from $V$ to $U$, is positive definite there, and $Q|_U$ inherits rationality, $(-1)^k$-symmetry and type orthogonality from $Q$. If $u\in U$ lies in the radical of $Q|_U$, then $Cu$ does too: type orthogonality gives $Q(Cx,y)=Q(x,C^{-1}y)$ for all $x,y$, since both sides select the same $(p,q)$-$(q,p)$ components, so $Q(Cu,U)=Q(u,C^{-1}U)=0$. Then $h(u,u)=Q(Cu,\bar u)=0$, and positive definiteness forces $u=0$; hence $Q|_U$ is nondegenerate and is a polarization of $U$. Step 2 (the orthogonal complement). As $Q|_U$ is nondegenerate, the rational equations $Q(x,U)=0$ define a rational complement $U^{\perp_Q}$ with $\dim U^{\perp_Q}=\dim V-\dim U$ and $U\cap U^{\perp_Q}=0$, so $V=U\oplus U^{\perp_Q}$. If $x=\sum x^{p,q}\in U^{\perp_Q}_{\mathbb C}$ and $v\in U^{q,p}$, then $0=Q(x,v)=\sum_{r,s}Q(x^{r,s},v)=Q(x^{q,p},v)$, because $Q$ pairs $V^{r,s}$ nontrivially only with $V^{s,r}$; as $x^{q,p}$ pairs nontrivially only with type $(q,p)$, it is orthogonal to all of $U$. Thus each $x^{p,q}\in U^{\perp_Q}$, which is therefore a rational sub-Hodge structure, and the restriction of $h$ to it is positive definite; by Step 1 the restricted $Q$ is a polarization of the complement. Step 3 (splitting, semisimplicity, scalar extension). In a short exact sequence $0\to U\to V\to W\to 0$ of polarizable structures the middle term $V$ is polarizable; identify $U$ with its image, a rational sub-Hodge structure because a bidegree-preserving map has bidegree-preserving image and kernel, and fix a polarization $Q$ of $V$. By Step 2, $\pi$ restricts to an isomorphism $U^{\perp_Q}\to W$ of Hodge structures whose inverse is the required section, so the sequence splits. For semisimplicity, choose in a nonzero polarizable $V$ a nonzero rational sub-Hodge structure $U$ of least dimension; $U$ is simple, and $V=U\oplus U^{\perp_Q}$ with polarizable complement of smaller dimension, so induction on $\dim V$ exhibits $V$ as a finite direct sum of simple structures. A rational splitting or direct-sum decomposition is given by rational matrices satisfying bidegree-wise linear identities (idempotence of the projections, and Q(x,U)=0 for the complement); these identities persist under scalar extension to any characteristic-zero field, so the splitting and the decomposition extend with it, and positivity is never invoked over that field.
items.axiom_use: Choice-free: the argument is finite-dimensional rational and complex linear algebra over fixed finite-dimensional structures; no choice principle is used.

items.title: Hodge–Riemann bilinear relations for smooth projective varieties
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), inherited from the analytic suppliers below. Let $X$ be a compact Kähler $n$-fold in the conventions of [[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]] and let $0\le k\le n$. On the primitive space $P^k$ put $$Q_k(a,b)=\epsilon(k)\int_Xa\wedge b\wedge\omega^{n-k}.$$ This form is $(-1)^k$-symmetric, pairs $P^{p,q}$ only with $P^{q,p}$, and for nonzero $a\in P^{p,q}$ satisfies $$i^{p-q}Q_k(a,\bar a)=(n-k)!\,\|a_{\mathrm{harm}}\|_{L^2}^2>0.$$ If $[\omega]=\ell\in H^2(X;\mathbb Q)$, then $Q_k$ is a rational polarization of $P^k$. Full $H^k$ is polarized by the orthogonal direct sum form that on $L^rP^{k-2r}$ is $(-1)^rQ_k$; degrees $k>n$ are polarized by transporting the polarization of $H^{2n-k}$ along $L^{k-n}$, with Tate shift. In particular this applies to smooth closed complex projective submanifolds of projective space with a hyperplane polarization, hence to smooth projective complex varieties through their smooth projective analytifications; more generally it applies to every real Kähler class, including $\ell+\epsilon\eta$ when represented by a positive closed form. For any continuous family of Kähler classes the primitive kernels (of every fixed degree $0\le k\le n$) vary continuously as subspaces; rational primitive spaces are asserted only at rational classes.
items.strategy: Assume AC. Route (Schnell, Class 18, §'The Hodge-Riemann bilinear relations', Theorem 18.15, printed pp. 5-6; Deligne, Théorie de Hodge II, (2.1.15)-(2.1.17), printed pp. 26-27; Demailly, Chapter VI §4 (4.4)-(4.6) for the projective instance). Step 1 (well-definedness, symmetry, types, positivity). If $b$ is closed and $a$ is replaced by $a+du$, the integrand changes by $d\bigl(u\wedge b\wedge\omega^{n-k}\bigr)$ up to sign, so the integral depends only on the cohomology classes by the general Stokes theorem [[thm-general-stokes-theorem]] and the de Rham comparison; the same argument applies in the second variable, and [[lem-rational-cohomology-scalar-comparison-for-compact-smooth-manifolds]] supplies the comparison maps. Wedge signs give $Q_k(b,a)=(-1)^kQ_k(a,b)$, and a class of type $(p,q)$ paired with one of type $(a,b)$ contributes only if $p+a+n-k=n=q+b+n-k$, i.e. $(a,b)=(q,p)$. Hard Lefschetz [[thm-kahler-identities-give-lefschetz-sl-two-and-hard-lefschetz]] identifies $P^k$ with the primitive harmonic $k$-forms, and the pointwise Weil-star identity of [[lem-hermitian-exterior-lefschetz-decomposition-and-weil-star-identity]] applied to the primitive form $\bar a$ of type $(q,p)$ gives $*\bar a=\epsilon(k)i^{p-q}L^{n-k}\bar a/(n-k)!$; integrating $a\wedge*\bar a$ (the $L^2$ inner product) yields $i^{p-q}Q_k(a,\bar a)=(n-k)!\|a\|^2>0$, the displayed positivity, and nondegeneracy. If $\ell$ is rational, [[lem-de-rham-top-integral-is-fundamental-class-evaluation]] and the cup-product compatibility identify $Q_k$ with $\epsilon(k)\langle a\smile b\smile\ell^{n-k},[X]\rangle$, a rational number on rational classes, so $Q_k$ is a rational polarization of $P^k$. Step 2 (the full cohomology form and the high-degree transport). Write a class of degree $k\le n$ as $a=L^ru$, $b=L^rv$ with $u,v$ primitive of degree $t=k-2r$. Since $\epsilon(k)=(-1)^r\epsilon(t)$, one has $Q_k(L^ru,L^rv)=(-1)^rQ_t(u,v)$; hence the form $(-1)^rQ_k$ on the summand $L^rP^{k-2r}$ equals $Q_t$ on primitive vectors, so its Weil form is the positive form of Step 1 and distinct string summands are orthogonal (for $r<s$ the integral contains $L^{n-k+r+s}u=L^{n-t+s-r}u=0$ by primitivity of $u$). The orthogonal direct sum over $r\ge\max(0,k-n)$ is therefore a rational polarization of $H^k$. For $k>n$ transport along the rational isomorphism $L^{k-n}:H^{2n-k}\to H^k$, which shifts both Hodge indices by $k-n$ and preserves the difference $p-q$ and the symmetry parity, so the transported form is again a polarization with the Tate shift of the conventions. Step 3 (the projective instance). The projective cases follow from Steps 1-2 applied to the compact Kähler manifold and rational class supplied by [[lem-smooth-projective-analytification-has-rational-kahler-polarization]]: for a smooth closed complex submanifold of projective space take the restriction of the Fubini-Study metric, and for a general smooth projective variety use the positive closed $(1,1)$-form representing the chosen ample rational class; in both cases the class is rational and the computations of Steps 1-2 apply verbatim. Step 4 (continuous variation). For fixed $0\le k\le n$ the map $A(\omega)=L^{n-k+1}:H^k\to H^{2n-k+2}$ has constant rank along Kähler classes: its rank is $\dim H^{k-2}$, a topological constant, by the primitive decomposition of Step 2 (zero when $k<2$). Selecting a nonvanishing maximal minor of its continuous matrix near a parameter and solving the pivot equations exhibits the kernel as the graph of a continuous family of matrices; this proves continuity of the primitive kernels. Positivity for each real Kähler class is the statement of Step 1 applied to that metric; continuity is not used to infer positivity at a limiting non-Kähler class. AC accounting: the suppliers [[lem-de-rham-top-integral-is-fundamental-class-evaluation]], [[lem-first-chern-form-agrees-with-the-topological-line-class]], [[lem-smooth-projective-analytification-has-rational-kahler-polarization]], [[thm-compact-kahler-hodge-decomposition-via-elliptic-harmonic-forms]] and [[thm-kahler-identities-give-lefschetz-sl-two-and-hard-lefschetz]] state AC; the general Stokes theorem assumes only $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, obtained from AC by [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]].

items.title: Polarized Hodge and hard Lefschetz package for smooth projective varieties
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), inherited from the suppliers below. For a smooth projective complex variety $X$ of pure dimension $n$ with a chosen ample line class $\ell\in H^2(X;\mathbb Q)$, its rational cohomology is finite-dimensional pure Hodge in each degree, functorial for pullback along holomorphic maps of the analytifications. Cup product has Hodge type $(0,0)$ and $\ell$ has type $(1,1)$. For $0\le k\le n$ the hard-Lefschetz maps $\ell^{n-k}:H^k\to H^{2n-k}$ are rational isomorphisms, and for $k>n$ so are their inverses $\ell^{k-n}:H^{2n-k}\to H^k$; the rational primitive summands satisfy the Hodge-Riemann positivity of [[thm-hodge-riemann-bilinear-relations-for-smooth-projective-varieties]], and the sign-adjusted full cohomology pairing is a rational polarization. Rational Hodge substructures split orthogonally. The same absolute positivity and hard-Lefschetz statements hold for real Kähler classes, and primitive kernels vary continuously along Kähler families. Rational splittings and isomorphisms persist after extension to any characteristic-zero field. This package does not supply weak hyperplane Lefschetz, relative hard Lefschetz, singular intersection-cohomology purity, or semisimplicity of arbitrary local systems.
items.strategy: Assume AC. Route: assemble the analytification, the compact Kähler Hodge theorem and the absolute Lefschetz package on the resulting compact Kähler manifold; source: Deligne, Théorie de Hodge II, (2.2.1), printed p. 27 (compact Kähler, 'par exemple projective lisse'), with Schnell, Class 18, Theorems 18.5, 18.13-18.15. Step 1 (Hodge structure and Hodge type). By [[lem-smooth-projective-analytification-has-rational-kahler-polarization]] the analytification $X^{\mathrm{an}}$ is a compact Kähler manifold and the class $\ell$ is the real image of an integral class represented by a positive closed $(1,1)$-form. The compact Kähler Hodge theorem [[thm-compact-kahler-hodge-decomposition-via-elliptic-harmonic-forms]] gives the finite-dimensional Hodge decomposition of each $H^k(X;\mathbb Q)$ and the functoriality and cup-product compatibility for holomorphic maps, while [[lem-rational-cohomology-scalar-comparison-for-compact-smooth-manifolds]] supplies the rational structure and its scalar extensions; the class $\ell$ has type $(1,1)$ by the positive closed $(1,1)$-form clause of [[lem-smooth-projective-analytification-has-rational-kahler-polarization]]. Step 2 (hard Lefschetz and polarization). [[thm-kahler-identities-give-lefschetz-sl-two-and-hard-lefschetz]] provides the rational hard-Lefschetz isomorphisms and primitive decomposition in degrees $\le n$, and [[thm-hodge-riemann-bilinear-relations-for-smooth-projective-varieties]] provides the primitive Hodge-Riemann positivity, the sign-adjusted full-cohomology polarization (including the transport for $k>n$) and the continuous variation of primitive kernels along Kähler families. [[lem-polarized-hodge-structures-have-orthogonal-semisimple-substructures]] then splits every rational sub-Hodge structure orthogonally. Both the splitting matrices and the Lefschetz matrices are rational, so they persist under extension to any characteristic-zero field, as proved in the two suppliers. Every conclusion is absolute in the stated degree; no relative, weak-Lefschetz, intersection-cohomology or local-system assertion is used.
items.axiom_use: Full AC is stated on the item and declared via [[def-axiom-of-choice]]; it is inherited from the analytification, Hodge-decomposition, hard-Lefschetz and rational-comparison suppliers.

items.title: Primitive one-forms and the Weil star sign
items.statement: With the conventions of [[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]]: on the oriented Euclidean two-plane with positively oriented orthonormal basis $e,f$, Kähler form $\omega=e\wedge f$ and compatible complex structure with $Je=f$, the type-$(1,0)$ form $u=e+if$ is primitive and satisfies $*u=-iu$. Its positive norm density is $u\wedge*\bar u=2\,e\wedge f$.
items.strategy: Choice-free finite-dimensional linear algebra; source: Schnell, Class 17, the $n=1$ case of the proof of Weil's identity and the two-plane table (printed pp. 3-4), and Schnell, Class 18, Theorem 18.15. Step 1 (primitivity and the star). The adjoint $\Lambda$ lowers degree by two, so $\Lambda u=0$ and $u$ is primitive; equivalently $L^{n-k+1}u=L^{1}u=0$ for $n=k=1$. The complementary-basis formula [[thm-hodge-star-exists-uniquely-and-has-the-orthonormal-basis-formula]] gives $*e=f$ and $*f=-e$, hence $*u=*e+i\,*f=f-ie=-i(e+if)=-iu$; this is the primitive-star formula of [[lem-hermitian-exterior-lefschetz-decomposition-and-weil-star-identity]] with $n=k=1$, $(p,q)=(1,0)$, namely $*u=\epsilon(1)i^{q-p}L^{0}u/(0)!=-iu$. Step 2 (the norm density). Since $\bar u=e-if$ is primitive of type $(0,1)$, the same formula gives $*\bar u=i\bar u$; and $u\wedge\bar u=(e+if)\wedge(e-if)=-2i\,e\wedge f$. Hence $u\wedge*\bar u=i\,u\wedge\bar u=2\,e\wedge f$, which is positive for the prescribed orientation. The verification consumes only the choice-free pointwise suppliers.
items.axiom_use: Choice-free: the verification is a finite-dimensional computation on a two-plane and consumes only the choice-free pointwise suppliers.
